- When sentiment turns positive (≥ 0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a 3–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 5+ days, model underestimates downward trend; add 2–3% upward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overpredicts mean reversion in short-term (1–3 day) horizons; adjust for lag by adding 1–2 days of smoothing or delay in turning points.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.16 to +0.4), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 2–3 day lag correction to avoid premature recovery.
- In low-volatility periods, model tends to overfit recent trends; reduce forecast sensitivity to recent 3–5 day moves.
